projects.name: On-Chip Filters for Hybrid Superconducting–Semiconducting Quantum Systems
projects.desc: Designed compact on-chip filters using niobium (Nb)-based coplanar waveguides on a silicon substrate to suppress 3–5 GHz microwave-photon leakage from an OCS transmon into nearby gate lines while preserving control signals up to 100 MHz. The design supports transmon-mediated coupling between triple quantum dots for scalable hybrid quantum-computing systems.

portfolio.objective: Create compact on-chip filtering that preserves gate-line control signals up to 100 MHz while isolating an OCS transmon operating from 3–5 GHz.
portfolio.challenge: Separate low-frequency control from microwave energy across room-temperature and cryogenic operation while minimizing passband insertion loss at a semiconductor–superconductor interface.
portfolio.contribution: Serve as technical owner for the filter subsystem; automate 3D models and HFSS simulations with PyAEDT, extract parasitics with Q3D, develop circuit models in AWR, and generate fabrication-ready GDS layouts.
portfolio.outcome: Produced compact niobium-on-silicon CPW filter layouts and fabricated devices for continued electromagnetic and cryogenic validation.

projects.name: Amplifier Module (22nm FinFET CMOS Tapeout)
projects.desc: Designed and simulated a 22 nm FinFET CMOS chip combining an analog amplifier, activation switches, and digital control logic, then completed the Cadence layout and DRC/LVS verification for tapeout.

portfolio.objective: Integrate an analog amplifier, activation switches, and digital control logic in a 22 nm FinFET CMOS tapeout.
portfolio.challenge: Coordinate analog performance, transistor-level control, physical-layout constraints, and verification in an advanced-node IC flow.
portfolio.contribution: Designed and simulated the circuit, completed the Cadence physical layout, and resolved Calibre DRC/LVS requirements for tapeout.
portfolio.outcome: Completed a tapeout-ready layout and verified more than 26 dB gain at 1 MHz with a 300 mV peak-to-peak output swing while operating 48% below the 500 µW power limit.

projects.name: Multi-IC solar charging module
projects.desc: Completed the system-level design, schematics, and PCB layout for a multi-IC solar-charging module.

portfolio.objective: Develop a multi-IC module that coordinates solar-energy input, charging, and board-level power delivery.
portfolio.challenge: Integrate multiple power-path components and interfaces into a coherent, buildable PCB design.
portfolio.contribution: Translated requirements into system architecture, designed and simulated buck, boost, and buck-boost power stages, completed schematics and PCB layout, and assembled SMD prototypes.
portfolio.outcome: Validated end-to-end circuit functionality with I²C communication, oscilloscopes, and electronic loads, and delivered the system design and board layout.
